Rooms.Name: Slag tunnel
Rooms.Description:
It is dark. Warm slag from the purging station comes continuously in
from the south. A little hole in the bottom of the tunnel leads down to
something, further down. Maybe it is worth a following... maybe not.

Exits.Description: The purging station.
Darkness.

Rooms.Name: Chute I
Rooms.Description: takes ...

Exits.Description: entrance 13111 ..
inside main extract 13119..
purging station 13153..
path of giants 13164..
upper mixing 13183..
time delay 13101..

Rooms.Name: A little grassy clearing
Rooms.Description:
The path comes in from the west and ends rather abruptly at a huge
and presumably very very deep hole in the ground. The edge of the hole
has been reinforced on one side so that you can approach without risking
a fall into it, at least not due to bad construction.

Exits.Description: A small path leads off.

Down a deep, deep hole.
- Going there is possible but just do not expect to get back up.
   At least, not this way.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The hole is 10 yards in diameter and quite smooth, at least as far
down as you can see. The sheer presence is a question in itself, and what
is it used for? There definitely is some kind of use for it as there
is a path up here. A small ladder goes down opposite the reinforced
edge.

The ladder is broken about a yard down. That means that there is or
was something down there. If you wait for it to be fixed you could find
a whole new world for you to explore. Or, you can try to use your well-
trained body and try to climb down the rather rugged surface of the hole.
Should not be too big of a problem for you.

Rooms.Name: Lesser used path of giants
Rooms.Description:
The caravan way of giants leads in a south-east direction even if its
travellers are somewhat less frequent than on the way in between the
high storages.

Exits.Description: The path ends in a small grassy field.
The small path continues.

Rooms.Name: Lesser used path of giants
Rooms.Description:
The caravan way of giants leads in a south-north direction even if
its travellers are somewhat less frequent than on the way in between the
high storages. A smaller trail leads off the path north towards
something else.

Exits.Description: The small path continues.
The path continues.

Rooms.Name: Chute V
Rooms.Description: DO not let any guard WALK out...

Rooms.Name: Rest and Dressing room
Rooms.Description:
Warm and friendly air seems to emanate both from north and south.
Right here, wooden panels cover the walls and warm marble covers the
floor. How they manage to keep the marble warm is a mystery to you, but
why complain and to whom? Some well-polished wooden benches stretch out
along the wall and there even are some hooks here for you to hang your
clothes. Behind the northern wooden door you hear laughter and random
splashes while from the south, soft dance music pours out and fills your
ears. There is a small sign hanging next to the stairway entrance to
this room.

Exits.Description: Steam slips out from under the door to the Sauna and Jacuzzis.
A constant flickering of light comes out from the lowered dance floor.
The stairs lead up to the VIP Lounge.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Your hostess Gretchen, invites YOU all to the Mill VIP club.
   Here there are no restrictions in age, gender or preferences.

                        WELCOME  and  ENJOY !!!

If you place your ear to the floor you can hear a weak sound
resembling flowing water. The heat must originate from some hot
springs or maybe someone has taken the effort to lead warm water through
the floor just to heat it up. Anything to make you feel good.

Rooms.Name: Sauna and Jacuzzi
Rooms.Description:
The heat and humidity is enormously high and the difference from the
Rest and Dressing room is extreme. This is where the VIPs of the mill
get started for their big parties. The evenings amusement take on new and
intriguing forms every time. Sometimes local employees and specially
invited guests join the event. This might become a new experience for
some, ancient history for others, but everyone seems to be happy.

Exits.Description: You can see the dressing room through the mist.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You read #<OE>LYT on a sign, which could be the brand name. Beware! It
is very hot and would surely burn a crude tattoo into your skin if you
happened to sit down on it.

Rooms.Name: Dance floor
Rooms.Description:
The dance floor is one of the smallest ones you have ever seen. It is
even smaller than the one at Granite Head's Bakery and he does not even
admit to having one. A crystal sphere rotates on its hanger in the
ceiling and some coloured lanterns have their flow of light directed
directly towards it, giving multicoloured reflections all over the room.
The few people here look up at you as the newbie you are, but they smile
invitingly towards you and bid you out on the small dancefloor. It
is always nice with a new face.

Exits.Description: The dressing room reveals itself through the dim lighting.

Rooms.Name: Hotter than Hot!!!
Rooms.Description:
One really should stop to think before one dives into a pool of smelt.
This time you only DIED!
It could have been worse.
You could have ended up eternally imprisoned in a metal block.
Or perhaps as a lethal part in a slaying weapon.
Not a nice future.
Consider yourself LUCKY!

Exits.Description: Someone put the plug in. You can not get out. What a pity.
To Late!

Rooms.Name: Road heading towards the Iron Mill
Rooms.Description:
The road surrounded by bushes turns west-north here allowing you to
either reach some large greyish buildings to the north or some more road
to the west. The buildings seem to let go of some smoke, smoke of the
same colour as the landscape around you.

Exits.Description:
You see a large sign in the distance. It has to be large, as you would
not see it this far away otherwise.
A bushed road leads away.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Dirty does not really bear good comparison with the real situation
here.
Just by barely touching a leaf or almost anything you get dirty and this
include trying to brush it away, as it only spreads it out more.

Dust and Dirt. The environmental issue does not seem to exist.
Perhaps that is the price for progress, perhaps not.

Rooms.Name: At a large Sign
Rooms.Description:
The road continues south toward the southern outskirts of the mill and
splits up west and east, heading for the large complex of very dirty
buildings in your view to the north. A large sign next to the road shows
that if you go in that direction you will end up being treated rather
hostile by the owners. They do not like trespassers. So you would better
stroll some other way or be prepared to encounter trouble.

Exits.Description: Further in between the mill buildings
The road goes on towards somewhere else.
Some big building towers up towards the dirty sky.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Dwarven Kingdom Iron Mill  a joint venture with
              Glob Inc. Development Group.


    Trespassers will be punished in the most severe manner.
            Minimum Removal Distance - Two Yards.

Rooms.Name: In between buildings
Rooms.Description:
One large grey building ends and another one begins. This has to be
the height of dwarven architecture. Add a little fog (smog) and your
sense of direction would go haywire. A little sign next to the western
door is still visible. Nothing seems to have stopped you so far so why
wait.

Exits.Description: In front of yet another large grey building.
Inside yet another large grey building.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The very dirty sign reads:

                    Prep Facility
           Preparation room and Mixing station


                 Do not feed the giants.
              (Unless you are supposed to)
There seems to be a shortage of that.   Hehe.    Sorry.

Rooms.Name: In front of a large grey building
Rooms.Description:
A little east-west path goes next to the wall of a huge grey
building. From its enormous chimney a thin chain comes down. Wonder what
they mean by 'For emergency use only - Unauthorized use will be punished
by DEATH!' as the sign next to it reads. These people really mean
business. The chain is climbable, at least upwards, but it looks a bit
unstable. And what was that thing about unauthorized use?

Exits.Description: A front a very huge door.
More grey buildings.
You can climb but it will not be popular.

Rooms.Name: At a HUGE gate
Rooms.Description:
You stand at the huge gate in an even larger building. The gate is so
large they had to split it up into two parts. A stream of air penetrates
the gate from the inside. It is warm and a bit dirty. A small sign with
a lot of writing on it is placed on the gate. You had better read it. If
you decide to not to enter the gate the yard stretches out in just about
any direction.

Exits.Description: It is warmer inside the building.
The huge gate continues.
You see the back side of a large sign along the path from the mill.
A grey building...

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
'GO AWAY!'
   'RAUS!'
   'STICK DIN FULA KOSSA!'
   'SKRID!'
   'VAI passear camelo'
... and a lot other more or less rude 'go away expressions'.

Rooms.Name: At a HUGE gate
Rooms.Description:

Exits.Description: It is warmer inside the building.

You see the backside of a large sign along the path from the mill.
The huge gate continues.

... and a lot other more or less rude 'go away expressions'.

Rooms.Name: End of a huge building
Rooms.Description:
Heaps of ashes and stone can be seen in abundance. The drawbacks of
development can be duly noted in the large amounts of trash and waste
that have been dumped here without any discrimination or regard for the
mountainside vegetation. A good suggestion would be to head west.

Exits.Description: A huge gate.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Stone that had its ore extracted is just waste. Apparently this is the
place where the dwarfs dump it, awaiting something better to do with it.

Rooms.Name: South wall inside the extraction house
Rooms.Description:
A variety of craftsman tools hangs on the walls as well as lie in
well-organised piles neatly stuffed away in the correct small toolboxes.
The temperature seems to increase in the northwards direction.

Exits.Description: A schlurping sound can be heard, but you can not see anything special.
A less organised corner.
The draft from the outside can be clearly noted in the aerosol flow.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Tools, tools, everywhere tools. Everything you, or anyone else would
ever need in order to run an iron mill staffed mainly by dwarfs is here
or out in the mill somewhere, but has its box here. Needless to say,
quite a lot of ladders have their places here.

Rooms.Name: Inside the Main Extraction building
Rooms.Description:
A huge hall stretches out in all directions but south, where the
large gate leads out into the fresher air. In the northern part of the
building a yellow-reddish glow can be seen at floor-level. The glow
appears to originate from the large chimney that goes from floor to roof
in the western part of the building and it ends abruptly in the
north-eastern corner of the building.

Exits.Description: A glow warms your face.
Outside, it is a bit colder but just as dirty.
Also inside the huge gate.

Rooms.Name: Inside the Main Extraction building
Rooms.Description:
A huge hall stretches out in all directions but south, where the large
gate leads out into the fresher air. In the northern part of the
building a yellow-reddish glow can be seen at floor-level. It appears to
originate from the large chimney that goes from floor to roof in the
western part of the building and ends abruptly in the north-eastern
corner.

Exits.Description: A glow warms your face.
Inside the huge gate.
Outside, it is a bit colder but just as dirty.

Rooms.Name: Inside the Main Extraction building
Rooms.Description:
West, you see a large platform above head-level from where you can
detect a faint swooshing sound. At ground level you can also walk
around the cigar-shaped chimney. The chimney seems to be very hot and
you hesitate to move in any closer, even though it should not be
dangerous. But you can always wimp out back east toward the gate.

Exits.Description: A faint glow warms your bared skin.
Next to a huge gate.
Next to the furnace.

Rooms.Name: Next to the blast furnace
Rooms.Description:
You stand under a small platform next to the blast furnace. A small
ladder lets you climb up to the platform. It is rather hot and
you wonder what makes the worker endure this environment. If it wasn't
for the high noise level and all the dirt the climate would be really
nice (if it wasn't for the dwarfs who keep on complaining about you
getting in the way all the time - Perhaps a large heap of sand and a few
big umbrella drinks would do the trick).

Exits.Description: The smelt outlet.
The draft from the outside can be clearly noted in the aerosol flow.
The southwest corner.
The platform.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
FIRE!!!
You see nothing but the scorching white heat of molten metal. Wonder how
they muster up that kind of temperature.

A metal grid allows you to walk around on a higher level of the
building.

Made up of bricks, its cigar shape surely has some process importance,
but you are not an extractive metallurgist. Then you would know. There
are some small windows one could look through to see the inside of the
furnace.

The ladder is very narrow - or maybe standard size for a midg..
                                                                dwarf.

Rooms.Name: Southwest corner of the main extraction building
Rooms.Description:
You stand under a small platform next to the blast furnace. It is
rather hot here and as everywhere else, a bit dirty too. A swooshing
sound can be heard intermittently from above the metal grid platform
above your head. There seems to something going on there.

Exits.Description: A corner.
A little ladder leads up to the platform.

Rooms.Name: Northwest corner of the main extraction building
Rooms.Description:
You stand under a small platform next to the blast furnace. It is
rather hot here but you ignore that as you see a very odd construct
placed on a rail here. The thing is apparently not in use right now but
the rail goes eastward if you want to activate it.

Exits.Description: The smelt outlet.
The south-western corner of the extraction building.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The complexity of the thingies indicates gnome workmanship, but
surprisingly it DOES seem to be working. The dwarfs would not have it
any other way so some bright dwarf must have had her hand into this
before it was taken on-line in the mill.

Rooms.Name: Smelt outlet
Rooms.Description:
Here the furnace is 'bled' of the molten metal. It plunges out of a
small hole in the furnace and splashes into a stream going eastward. A
small rail starting right under the hole goes out in an arch towards the
west.

Exits.Description: The smelt flows away.
A little ladder goes up the furnace.
Follow the rail to the solution.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The plug fits perfectly in the furnace hole. The mill staff uses it to
halt the flow of metal once in a while or as there is a need for it.
It leads west of here. Wonder what the use of it is.

Ooohh, so very hot. Melting metal in that inferno must be child's
play. But you DO wonder how they do it.  The flowing smelt is sooo sexy -
You stay and admire it for a while.  Why did you not learn about this in
school?
 Sigh.

Rooms.Name: Next to the smelt flow
Rooms.Description:
A small channel in the floor conducts the smelt in an eastward
direction. The smelt seems to be covered with some slag that surely
would ruin the fine iron if left on and in the metal. You can
follow the flow east-west or you can head towards the south and the exit
out of the building.

Exits.Description: There is some kind of blocker in the smelt flow.
You can see the dirt in the air whirl at the huge gate.
The smelt outlet!

Rooms.Name: Slag Scraper
Rooms.Description:
Here the slag is scraped off from the smelt coming from the west. All
of the slag it seems, by some large doctors blade. Some small amount of
pure metal is scraped of too, but that is just to be on the safe side.
The off-scraped is turned into a small channel leading primarily north.
The rest of the now clean smelt continues east.

Exits.Description: The slag channel leads away the slag.
The metal flows on.
The metal comes flowing.

Rooms.Name: Slag Channel
Rooms.Description:
The slag comes in from the scrapes in the south and slowly follows
the channel here to where it plunges down into some black hole in the
floor.

Exits.Description: More slag comes from the scraper.
The slag tank accepts all kind of trash and will keep it safe.

Rooms.Name: Slag Tank
Rooms.Description:
Its warm, DARK, without exit and there is absolutely no magic in this
place. What did you think of when you jumped into this place. You had
better stay and contemplate your situation for a while before you start
whining about rescue. Perhaps some study of the slag heaps down here
is something to do while being stuck.

Exits.Description:
It is far away and more hot slag keeps on coming, effectively
hindering you from going up again. Your only chance is to pray to the
gods that be to take you home again.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Slag is no good. Well perhaps maybe as roadfill. Well maybe it is
good. Slagbuilders are added to the furnace setup to create a slag with
wanted, specific properties. But what is slag then, you ask yourself as
you sit there having a real dull time? Slag is a complex gathering of
mostly oxides that bond the real unwanted stuff in the smelt to itself in
a way that makes it, at least somewhat, easily removable before the smelt
reaches the foundry. Neat, is it not?

Rooms.Name: Next to the smelt flow
Rooms.Description:
A small channel in the floor conducts the smelt in an eastward
direction. The smelt is free from any kind of impurities and is now
ready to continue to alloying and final treatment. The big building you
are in also stretches out southwards.

Exits.Description: The lighting change at the huge gate.

Rooms.Name: Scrap corner
Rooms.Description:
Broken tools, empty barrels and a lot more are scattered around in
this place. It seems that the things have been here for years but the
dirt in the mill easily covers up any proof of that. As the building
expands to the north and west the scrap density clearly decreases.

Exits.Description: The world seems more organised.
The world seems more organised.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Tools, tools, everywhere tools. All and everything you, or someone
else, would ever need in order to run a iron mill populated mainly of
dwarves is here or is out in the mill somewhere but have their boxes
here. Needless to say quite a lot of ladders have their place here.
Unfortunately these items and boxes no longer seem to be used. They
almost look abandoned.

Rooms.Name: The smeltpath plunges down
Rooms.Description:
The smelt falls down through a hole on the channel to some sublevel
part of the plant. The sound of it splashing into the collector below is
fascinating. The intriguing sound fights the urge to explore further but
you loosen yourself from its grip and start to search for some stairs to
descend, which is not easy as the building expands into all directions.

Exits.Description: The smelt comes running.

Schluurrrrp!!!
The darkness gleams, but there is no way down for you here.

Rooms.Name: East of the plunging path
Rooms.Description:
The temperature is a bit lower here compared with next to the westly
smelt but the dirt is still here. A small spiral staircase is north of
you.

Exits.Description: A small flight of stairs comes up from below.
A lot of junk is piled up here for you to sort out.
The smelt flow ends and a schlurping sound can be heard.

Rooms.Name: North of the plunging path
Rooms.Description:
The temperature is a bit lower here compared with next to the southern
smelt but the dirt is still here. A small spiral staircase is east of
you.

Exits.Description: A small windle of stairs comes up from below.
The smelt flow ends and a schlurping sound can be heard.

Rooms.Name: Windle of stairs
Rooms.Description:
Stairs go down to the foundry on the floor below this level of the
iron mill. Steam and smoke come blowing up through the metal grid steps.
The humidity down there must be enormous. Perhaps you should stay up
here and troop off south or west into the big building.

Exits.Description:
The air coming from below is warm and humid. Perhaps they have a sauna
down there.

Rooms.Name: Up on a shelf - SouthEast corner.
Rooms.Description:
You can see through the metal grid making up the floor you stand on.
The view over the mill inside is rather disappointing. The place has
not been cleaned for ages it seems, but on the other hand you should not
be in here in the first place, so who should you complain to? Some kind
of air pumping device is here awaiting to be served.

Exits.Description: More grid.
More grid.
A tiny winy ladder leads down.

Rooms.Name: Up on a shelf - SouthWest corner.
Rooms.Description:
You can see through the metal grid, making up the floor you stand on.
The view over the mill inside is rather disappointing. The place has
not been cleaned for ages it seems, but on the other hand you should not
be in here in the first place, so who should you complain to? Some kind
of air pumping device is here awaiting to be served.

Exits.Description: More grid.
More grid.

Rooms.Description:

More grid.

Rooms.Description:

The view over the mill inside is rather disappointing. The place has

Exits.Description: More grid.
More grid.

Rooms.Name: Inside an air pump
Rooms.Description:
The hole in the floor that you came in through and the walls are
covered with some VERY reinforced paper lining. The lining must be very
magic as the air elementals kept in here can not escape. In the
narrow end you can see the inside of the furnace where the metal is
produced.

Exits.Description: YOU can step down on the grid.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
FIRE FIRE FIRE!!!
The air coming from the pump burns away the carbon in the furnace setup
producing a large portion of the heat needed to produce the liquid iron.

Rooms.Name: Finance and Public Relations Department
Rooms.Description:
Welcome to the finance department of the Dwarf Kingdom & Glob
Incorporated joint venture Iron Mill. The air in here is much fresher
than in the rest of the mill which makes you hesitate about going out
east again. North is a room for displaying charts and figures. West
you should be able to hear the steady work of the department staff.

Exits.Description: The display room.
Not nearly as clean as in here.
A hallway.

Rooms.Name: Chart and display room
Rooms.Description:
Along the walls are a multitude of charts and graphs showing you the
latest production and sale statistics, efficiency ratings, upkeep,
salary costs, gain after taxation with or without various deductions and
bla bla bla... You quickly grow bored and check for exits. On your way
back out you can pass the compulsory step-by-step ore-to-metal view
box that every decent mill must have.

Exits.Description: Freedom of statistics. HURRAY!!!!

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
In this mill iron is produced with help of a rather standard
continuous counter flow reactor, The Blast Furnace. In it the ferrous ore
is loaded together with a mix of limestone and coal/coke in the top.
Initially the mix is dried up after which preheating takes place a bit
further down the furnace. Next the carbon in the mix and the carbon
monoxide produced lower in the furnace starts to reduce the iron oxide
to a lesser oxide Hematite -> Magnetite  ->  Wüstite  ->  pure liquid
IRON. At the bottom of the furnace the added air burns the leftover of
the carbon giving away enormous heat to manage the final melting. A
continuous separation of molten metal and slags from the furnace is also
done very low in the furnace.

Furball, Glob Inc. Research Department.
in association with B-#<AA>, your local metallurgist and mountainman.

Rooms.Name: Accountant office
Rooms.Description:
The office has no windows but instead a large desk in the centre with
a comfortable chair behind and two (less comfy) chairs in front. A huge
archive file cabinet flanks the desk. There really is not any more
furniture in here, if you do not count the constant piles of paper that
always seem to be gathering.

Exits.Description: A small door leads out to the plain hallway.
The floor can be lifted up to expose a little stairwell.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Its huge. Unfortunately for the accountant it is filled with paperwork.
Looks about as dull as it is. Numbers and words make a big mumbo jumbo.

Rooms.Name: Assistant secretary desk
Rooms.Description:
A secretary's desk is placed here in the hallway and is the centre of
all work being done in here. North is the Assistant Managers office
while the accountant has his south of here. On the desk there are two
small baskets, one marked #wout#W and one marked #win#W. The chair
behind the desk looks very little used, a sign of the magnitude of the
secretary's workload.

Exits.Description: A sign on the door says 'Assistant Manager'.
A hallway.
A sign on the door says 'Accountant'.
A hallway.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The IN box is very filled. Poor secretary.

The OUT box is empty. Guess the secretary has to run over with the
papers immediately to please her employers.
The desk is a mess. No time to organise anything here, nono.

Rooms.Name: Manager assistant Room
Rooms.Description:
The size and shape of this room is like all the others in the Finance
Department. Walls with no windows but with calming wallpaper covering
them, a large desk in the centre with a comfortable chair behind and two
(less comfy) chairs in front. And not to forget the standard issue
triple archive file cabinet for all useful documents he might ever need.
The amount of paper on his desk is of course also a bit too high to be
pleasurable.

Exits.Description: A plain door leads out to the hallway.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
You do feel calmer as you look at the wallpaper.  Little globs swim
through a serene blue sea.

Papers papers - everywhere papers. Wonder how he notices any new
papers, or perhaps that is what he does not do...

Rooms.Name: VIP Lounge and coffee room
Rooms.Description:
This room differs from the rest as it is much bigger. Along two
of the walls go two enormous sofas. Next to the sofas are some low
tables. On the other side of the tables sit low leather armchairs. They
would be perfect in every adventurers' home to relax in after a long
hard day of questing. The third wall in covered with some complex
apparatus of evidently gnomish design smelling strongly of coffee. The
southwest corner seems strangely cleared but the rest of the room is
real comfortable.

Exits.Description:
A hallway. There would be no problems in closing up that door, if such a
need arise.
You hear a faint humming as of music. Sounds intriguing.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Nice low table and on the table, Cookies!!!, but a-a-a they are not
for you, so hands off.

What a delight it would be to relax in this wonderful piece of
furniture. Apperantly a gift from someone in the court of Galadriel as
it clearly has elvish design.
AHA! A trapdoor going down.

Rooms.Name: Managers secretary desk
Rooms.Description:
A small desk stands next to the end of the hallway. On it three small
cages stand. In, Out and Manager. There are not too many papers in either
of them. There also is a small carpet lying in front of the wooden door
to the north.

Exits.Description: A small sign on the door says 'MANAGER'.
A hallway.
The VIP room. At least it says so in the door.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
So very clean. Guess she polishes her desk as much as her
fingernails.
The OUT box is empty. All done and delivered.
The IN box is empty. No more to do.
The Manager box is empty.

What can I say.
A real nice carpet but only for manager feet. So STEP OFF!

Rooms.Name: Mill Manager Office
Rooms.Description:
A magnificent office, huge one-piece marble desk and accordingly the
most throne like office chair you have ever seen, behind it. Even the
guest chairs look inviting. A small fireplace is moulded into the west
wall. There are even paintings on the walls. They mostly show panoramic
views of the mill, but still no one else in the finance department dares
to have any.

Exits.Description: A small door.
A hallway.

The fireplace is made up of bricks but there is no wood in it. No
ashes either. Seems like something else makes up the heat in here.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
BIG (well he is a dwarf) and made out of one single slab of marble.
That sure was not free. Guess the operating results are pretty good.

The bigger the chair and chair backsupport the more important
position one holds. Big chair and backsupport almost to the roof.
 Top of the Pops.

The fireplace is made up of bricks but there is no wood in it. No
ashes either. Seems like something else makes up the heat in here.

Mill panoramas how, ehhhh, nice. A lot of dirty buildings and small
workers. Good artist though, but with a very boring motif.
The door to the closet is powerful but the lock is broken... Oh no!!!

Rooms.Name: Below the stairs
Rooms.Description:
Heat makes your face red as you look toward the pool south of here
where the smelt splashes down from above. A beautiful piece of liquid
metal magic. Either head toward the metalfall or up the stairs.

Exits.Description: A metal pool and a very odd 'waterfall'.
A windle of stairs take you up.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The windle of stairs is pretty small. It is a Dwarven iron mill.

Rooms.Name: Metal pool
Rooms.Description:
The molten metal comes pouring down through a hole in the roof.
A quite hazardous place. If a working condition inspector ever made it
here alive (and out again) he would close this place immediately or at
least try to. Letting iron smelt touch your bare hand will scorch
you completely and give you agony for a long time. Better be careful.

Exits.Description: A small windle of stairs go up.
A rather smoky room.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The spectacular view is so wonderful you have to convince yourself
very hard not to get too close...

Rooms.Name: Purging Station
Rooms.Description:
This is where air is forced through the smelt pool to draw out any
unwanted elements that lie invisible in the smelt. It is quite a smoky
room as the ventilation, if there ever was any, is nonfunctional. A
tilting scraper goes across the surface in a regular pattern removing
the slag as it appears. The sound level is quite high as the purging is
a very noisy thing. A small slurp adds to the sound as the slag goes
down into a small hole to the north.

Exits.Description: Darkness is very much present in the slag tunnel leading off.
The metal flows to another pool.
A glowing waterfall can be seen.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The air elementals usually flow through the smelt dragging along the
unwanted elements with them as they come up to the surface again.

Rooms.Name: Alloying pool
Rooms.Description:
To give the metal its specific properties, the dwarfs shovel some
secret alloying additives into the smelt pool. What alloy to add and when
is a highly guarded secret and you can see that the alloying rooms north
and south are usually very well guarded. The stream of smelt that come in
from the west continues eastwards as a melt.

Exits.Description: A very dirty alloy storage room.
The stream of melt splits up.
A rather clean alloy storage room.
Another pool.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Watch out!  A splash of melt and you will burn. Be careful.

Rooms.Name: Alloy Room
Rooms.Description:
Tall heaps of grubble are lying everywhere. Small signs written in
some dwarfish code system are posted above the heaps. Small openings
in the wall allow for the supply system to replenish the supply of
alloying elements, very practical. There is a bit of a distance out to
the alloying pool, guess that is where the guards usually hang out.

Exits.Description: A metal pool.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The very small openings lead to large but unavailable storage rooms
for the bulk mass of the alloys.

Do you know this dwarf code system???
        I did not think so!
      Do not mess it up, OK?!!

Rooms.Name: Alloy Room
Rooms.Description:
Small metal bars lie in well organized heaps, strictly tagged with a
sign in some secret dwarven code system. Perhaps if you interrogate the
alloyer enough he will tell you what it means but you are not sure even
he knows. He just follows directives given to him. Perhaps you could do
some testing of the bars yourself but your metallurgical skills are
non-existant, so it would probably not turn out very well. There is a bit
of a distance out to the alloying pool, guess that is where the guards
usually hang out.

Exits.Description: A metal pool.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The bars are not of iron origin that you can establish, but what they
really are made of, you have no clue about.

Rooms.Name: Melt splitter
Rooms.Description:
The meltflow coming in the floor from the west is split up here into
three different streams flowing north, east and south and then down to
the foundry. A very hot cylinder distributes the melt in the supposed
directions. Touching without the correct protection would easily cause
serious burn to your hands.

Exits.Description:
The stream of metal reaches the foundry and nothing but steam comes
back up from down there.

The stream of metal reaches the foundry and nothing but steam comes
back up from down there.

The stream of metal reaches the foundry and nothing but steam comes
back up from down there.
A metal pool.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Turning the cylinder cause two of the melt outlets to be blocked
allowing melt from the inflow to go only in one direction. Perhaps the
foundry wants their moulds filled up quickly and intermittently.

Rooms.Name: Foundry
Rooms.Description:
This is the part of the mill where the melt solidifies under some kind
of controlled environment. The humidity is so intense that you feel
your clothing dampening on you every second you stay. The production
logistics are quite complex with melt coming in and filling up small
moulds which solidify after being touched by water elementals that
usually roam around in here. The melt comes in from up above and the ready 
bars are taken out eastly.

Exits.Description: The bar storage.
More steam comes from another part of the Foundry.
The meltsplitter takes melt your way.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The mould are about as big as the bars. What a surprise!

Rooms.Name: Foundry
Rooms.Description:
This is the part of the mill where the melt solidifies under some kind
of controlled environment. The humidity is so intense that you feel
your clothing dampening on you every second you stay. The production
logistics are quite complex with melt coming in and filling up small
moulds which solidify after being touched by water elementals that
usually roam around in here. The melt comes in from up above and the ready 
bars are taken out eastly.

Exits.Description: More steam comes from another part of the Foundry.
The bar storage.
The meltsplitter takes melt your way.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The mould are about as big as the bars. What a surprise!

Rooms.Name: Foundry
Rooms.Description:
This is the part of the mill where the melt solidifies under some kind
of controlled environment. The humidity is so intense that you feel
your clothing dampening on you every second you stay. The production
logistics are quite complex with melt coming in and filling up small
moulds which solidify after being touched by water elementals that
usually roam around in here. The melt comes in from up above and the ready 
bars are taken out eastly.

Exits.Description: More steam comes from another part of the Foundry.
The bar storage.
More steam comes from another part of the Foundry.
The meltsplitter takes melt your way.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The mould are about as big as the bars. What a surprise!

Rooms.Name: Bar Storage
Rooms.Description:
You have entered a huge room filled with still warm metal bars of
equal size. There appears to be no difference between them but you have
good reason to think that the ancient dwarf magic of the blacksmiths
could change that quite a lot. The bar origin can be found to the west
in the foundry while there seems to be some kind of transport out of
this location to the south of here.

Exits.Description: An occasional grunt can be heard.
Hot steamy air pour out from the foundry.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Geeeeee, even if you could count, you could still not count to this
many...

Rooms.Name: Pick up room
Rooms.Description:
Giants come to this place to pick up metal bars to carry them in
their slow caravan towards some distant place. The giant controller that
also work as a bar counter has his chair here. It is worth noticing that
the ground is filled with small holes. Either some groundhog tribe did
this or the giants overloaded themselves and discarded the excess. North
the bar storage take up the major part while a path goes up and away.

Exits.Description:
You see a high storage of bars and bars and bars and bars...
(Too sad you can not order a single beer at any of them.)
A trail leads off.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The chair is elevated a few meters above the ground. Prolly to be
able to get in closer to the head of the carrier giants.

Rooms.Name: Path of giants
Rooms.Description:
The caravan way of the giants goes east towards some distant place or
down to the mill pick up room. Grunts and metallic clashes can be heard
as new loads get ready below you. The path you are on is well trodden
and takes you between two distant high storages. Dull - true, but
efficient - yes.

Exits.Description: The path continues.
A pick up room for metal bars.

Rooms.Name: Path of giants
Rooms.Description:
The caravan way of the giants either leads in from the east and trails
off to the north or vice versa. The path is well trampled and leads you
between two distant high storages. Dull - true, but efficient - yes.

Exits.Description: The path continues.
The path continues.

Rooms.Name: Path of giants
Rooms.Description:
The caravan way of the giants either leads in from the south and goes
off to the east or vice versa. The path is well trodden and leads you
between two distant high storages. Dull - true, but efficient - yes.
Strangely enough a little path trails off to the north. It looks still
in use.

Exits.Description: The path continues somewhat lesser used.
The path continues.
The path continues.

Rooms.Name: Path of giants
Rooms.Description:
The caravan way of the giants either takes you north or to the west
depending on your travel direction. The path available is well trampled
and leads you between two distant high storages. Dull - true, but
efficient - yes.

Exits.Description: A drop room.
The path continues.

Rooms.Name: Drop room
Rooms.Description:
This is where the carrier giants that usually come in from the south
should leave the metal bars for the blacksmiths' attendants to pick them
up and bring them into the smithery to the east. As the giants are not
always too careful (or bright) the signs of many depressions in the
ground are clearly visible. The bars do not get hurt from this drop but
it is not recommended to stay here long as your skull most probably
would not like the experience of the full impact of a metal bar
from giant height.

Exits.Description: A door leads into the House of Blacksmiths.
A path leads off.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Deep.
 Standing in the way of that drop would have been clearly fatal.

Rooms.Name: Secret treasury
Rooms.Description:
One demand from the investors was that an ATM should be placed at the
mill to ensure secure handling of their money. With the right
connections and some serious bribes the mill was the first ever to be
allowed to set up an ATM outside Midgaard town.

Exits.Description: Light comes down from the accountant's office.

Rooms.Name: Secret closet
Rooms.Description:
Everyone has something to hide. Some bury it in the forest, others
deep in the sea, yet others secretly sneak it into poems that everyone
can read but no one can understand. This is another common place whereto
shovel in your old skeletons - into the old closet, lock and then hide
the key forever.

Exits.Description: The manager office is so close.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: The door is powerful but the lock is broken....  oh no!!!

Rooms.Name: Inside the reheating furnace
Rooms.Description:
Scorching hot this place. Ouch!!! You jump around as a little
panicked cricket inside a jar wildly shaken by a curious child. Why did
you go here in the first place? Get out before you start burning.
                   Quick! Quick! Quick!

Exits.Description:
If you want to walk on burning coal here is your chance. It wont hurt.
Much.

If you want to walk on burning coal here is your chance. It wont hurt.
Much.

If you want to walk on burning coal here is your chance. It wont hurt.
Much.

If you want to walk on burning coal here is your chance. It wont hurt.
Much.
Up the chimney there is no hot coal to bother your sore feet with.

Rooms.Name: Entrance
Rooms.Description:
Right inside from a western door. From the other side frequent grunts
and moans can be heard as well as a sporadic metallic crash. You sense a
slight heat coming from the east. It has to be more comfortable there
than in this drafty place.

Exits.Description: Warmth meets you if you travel inside the Smithery.
The bar storage.

Rooms.Name: Coal store
Rooms.Description:
*Cough!*Cough!!* The Coal dust not only stains your clothes it makes
you sneeze as well which roars up more dust that makes you sneeze and
dirties you clothing even further. Better leave this place while you
still can find the exit.

Exits.Description: A fire allows for reheating of the metal.

Rooms.Name: Blast Reheater
Rooms.Description:
Before the blacksmiths do their trick on the metal bars from the mill
they need to be red hot. The fireplace or the blast reheater is the
place for that. The coal is stored in a coalstorage to the north, black
footprints clearly show that. Westward is the exit out to the bar
storage and from the east the continuous banging from the blacksmith can
be heard all day.

Exits.Description: Darkness meets you.
An anvil stands there, ready for use.
The entrance to the Blacksmiths.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The fireplace is built up by bricks, and in the centre of it carbon
brickets feed the fire to extreme temperatures. You can enter it if you
want to but there is a good chance that the fire might scorch you a bit.
Dwarf sized and very, very black.

Rooms.Name: Display room
Rooms.Description:
All over the room there are the most incredible swords, armours and
gadgets useful in warfare. Unfortunately most of them are in size XS, but
some, more dull looking, come in bigger sizes. Apparently the objects go
in steps from the blacksmith, first the polisher goes over them east of
here and then they are sold in the Shoppe south. A small sign stands
next to the door on the western wall.

Exits.Description: A slight scent of solvents traces themselves to you.
Weaponry and Armoury Shoppe.
The air seems much fresher in there...

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Whoooaa, there is a lot of stuff in here.
Guess the shop has a potential for some real interesting sales...

The little sign reads :

   Finance and Public Relations Department

Rooms.Name: Weaponry and Armoury Shoppe counter of the Blacksmiths
Rooms.Description:
You do not have that much money. Why did you burn all in the Hide 'n
Tooth shop? Those are the first thoughts that go through your mind
when looking at all these marvellous pieces of equipment that are up on
display here. Dwarf size dolls all dressed up for war in well polished
armour stand everywhere. If you are a dwarf, you are in Utopia.

Exits.Description: A display room.

The dwarven settlement should appear in front of you if leave the shop
taking the chute westly. But beware, to avoid the sneaky attempt of
local trash a one way door has been installed. You can not climb back up
again.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Sorry, it is pay #ybefore#N view that is the rule here.

Rooms.Name: Smithy's
Rooms.Description:
A large anvil takes up the center part of this place. Pieces of
metal lie scattered around in various degrees of development. Could this
place really be where all magnificent dwarven wartools originate?  Maybe
so. It does not look that wrong. The metal is heated up at the furnace
to the west and after proper treatment it goes either south to the
polisher or, hopefully not, east to the trash corner.

Exits.Description: BIG DOOR -- BIG SIGN -- BIG LETTERS -- 'GO AWAY!!!'.
The trash corner.
You smell a faint touch of solvents reach you from that room.
The furnace heatens the metal pieces.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Big chunk of metal, with a flat upper side. Perfect for whacking your
hammer against or perhaps some poor old opponents head...

Rooms.Name: Trash corner
Rooms.Description:
Very deformed versions of what seems to be excellent armour lie just
slumped on the floor. There really is nothing wrong with them that you
can see but they must have failed the scrutinizing eyes of their
creator.  A large sign hangs on the wall. The Smithy's place is to the
west.

Exits.Description: Bank! Bonk! Smash! Can be heard when the smith is at work.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: TOUCH AND DIE!!!

Rooms.Name: Polishing room
Rooms.Description:
What would the sales people say if the gear was not in top notch
shape and perfectly stainless? A diverse collection of polishes fill the
room, causing the smell of abrasives and polish mixes that fills the
air, to totally block your sensory system in this clean environment.

Exits.Description: Oh, was there a little pink elephant in the corner?!!
Hi there little wallie. Wanna be friends?
OH NOOOOO. IT IS COMING TO GET ME!!!!!!
Do Be Do Be Do Be Dooooooo! Hey! This is fun! Sing along! Tralalala!
Worms, worms, worms... and more worms...
No floor. Odd. Could bet there was a floor there just a second ago.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: Do not inhale to long. Could get permanent damage from those...

Rooms.Name: Grand-Smiths room
Rooms.Description:
You can feel the magic in this room. Here the dwarven master
blacksmith has formed the most perfect and powerful equipment of
war that you could ever imagine. There is a small blast furnace here too
so that there will be no need to leave during complex enchantments to
reheat the masterpiece-to-be. A certain room to the north has been
assigned to the hardening of weaponry while the final tests of the
equipment are done east of here. If a piece is not accepted as a base for
an item it is utterly dismissed west to the big reheater.

Exits.Description: Hardening room.
Test room.
A plain door leads out. Keep it closed.
Go with the discards to the reheater.

What was that? It seemed like a big eye in the midst of the blackened
ceiling just closed itself as you started looking up. That just can not
be true, can it?

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It looks as if you have stumbled over something previously unknown. Up
in the stone above, unreachable for you (even with the aid of magics,
strangely enough) you can now see the faint outline of a closed eyelid.
What terrible organization or entity can it be that have such power to
peek into the most holy of dwarven places.

Studying the eyelid you also notice a even fainter carving around where
the eye is. It appears triangular. But who uses a triangle around a eye
as a insignia?
OH NO!!! It is the Glob Inc insignia  -  RUN!!!  -  FLEE!!!

Very little is actually known about this society. Perhaps it is best
not to know too much. Very few outsiders that know anything true about it
are still alive. Just for your own sake, perhaps you should ignore this
eye, as they most certainly already know that you have been studying it.

Rooms.Name: Hardening room
Rooms.Description:
To give the weapons extra edge in combat, the dwarfs harden them. The
procedure usually is to quickly cool the red hot metal in oil or salted
water, but sometimes for that very special power-kick to that very
special weapon, a more alternative hardening method is used. That is why
there usually are slaves here of different species, waiting...
You could place yourself first in line and become a nice addition.

Exits.Description: Grand-Smiths room.

Rooms.Name: Test room
Rooms.Description:
All equipment coming out from the Grand Master Smiths hands must be
duly tested for one to truly find the clear potential of the individual
items. This room has experienced many of those tests. Usually on
non-willing victims. Their pain and agony can still be felt in the
walls.  Not a very pleasant room to be in, unless you should test
something. For that purpose some crude X-crosses are usually placed
here.

Exits.Description: Grand-Smiths room.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: You can truly feel the pain. Not nice at all, unless you are a demon.

Rooms.Name: Entry to Prep facility
Rooms.Description:
East of here is an open area in front of a huge building with a fat
chimney. Westwardly some grinding and smashing sounds increase in
volume.

Exits.Description: A small door probably leads out of the building.
A rather empty room.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
Another big grey building. Who was the architect, you really would
like to talk to him.

Rooms.Name: Upper mixing station
Rooms.Description:
A metal grating covers a wide hole in the ground. Large heaps of some
grey and some black stuff are blended with a slightly larger heap of
finely crushed stone. What could drive the dwarves to shovel all this
down
through the bars is still a question to you. In all directions but east,
large still-to-be-mixed masses pile up in storage rooms.

Exits.Description: Darkness.
Nothing but a way out.
Whiteness.
Greyness and a bit of grunting.
It is rather dark down there but a grinding sounds can be clearly heard.

Rooms.Name: Limestone deposit
Rooms.Description:
Whiteish powders fill this room to the very brim. No space is spared
and anything or anyone entering this room gets its share on itself. It
is not poisonous but prolonged exposure and inhalation could damage your
health. Which the workers that usually are around here have noticed. More
white powder comes pouring out from a hole in the wall above you.

Exits.Description: The mixing station.
Some larger storeroom seems reachable up there.

ExtraDescriptions.Description: It sure looks like one could climb up there if one wanted too.

Rooms.Name: Upper Limestone deposit
Rooms.Description:
A grinding wheel blocks any further progress upwards. Through the
wheel a whitish powder slowly falls down upon anyone stupid enough
to stand under it (i.e. you).  You'd better leave. This can not be
healthy, even if its not directly dangerous.

Exits.Description: It is a bit too dirty to see anything down there.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
It is big. It is lethal to tamper with. Just accept that it grinds
the limestone to powder making it much more easier to handle.

Rooms.Name: Coal store
Rooms.Description:
This room is covered in blackness, as all light is banned from here
due to the risk of explosion and the fact that the coal is very light
absorbing. A fireball in here would not be recommended for anyone
within a few hundred yards.

Exits.Description: The mixing station - take a shovel and help with the shovelling.

Rooms.Name: Ore Store
Rooms.Description:
Fine grain ore / stone lies everywhere as sharp shards. You have to
be extra careful if you want to walk round in this place without
damaging your feet or your equipment. The crushing sounds from the west
have definitely increased and it seems that the crushed stone really
just is transported through this place on its way to the eastern mixing
station.

Exits.Description: The mixing station. Do not change the amount. Would be bad for the iron.

You see shards of stone whirl about as the big blocks are being
crushed.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The stoneshards are very sharp and your warlike mind immediately
starts to think about ways to convert this to weaponry. But its only
shards, not much one can do but walk on it.

Rooms.Name: Ore Crushing Area [Enter at own risk]
Rooms.Description:
Stones in widely varied sizes lie scattered around in what seems to
be a totally devastated area. No vegetation is still alive in here
after the treatment the giants have given this place. The ground is
covered with shards and you must be very careful not to cut yourself if
you want to walk around in here. On the other hand, if you stay long
enough maybe some giants will want to give you some of their special
treatment. You can flee this place out to the east or continue your
perilous journey west or south further into Giant crushing lands.

Exits.Description: Bring some readycrushed ore to the mixing station.
Ore Crushing Area [Enter at own risk].
Ore Crushing Area [Enter at own risk].

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The stoneshards on the ground and on nearby larger stones but into
you draining your blood and trashing your clothes. Maybe you should do
like the giants and get some revenge on the stone around you. The
dwarven workers would like some extra, free, personnel too.

Rooms.Name: Ore Crushing Area [Enter at own risk]
Rooms.Description:
Stones in widely varied sizes lie scattered around in what seems to
be a totally devastated area. No vegetation is still alive in here
after the the treatment the giants have given this place. The ground is
covered with shards and you must be very careful not to cut yourself if
you want to walk around in here. On the other hand, if you stay long
enough maybe some giants will want to give you some of their special
treatment. The crushing area expands further north and west.

Exits.Description: Ore Crushing Area [Enter at own risk].
Ore Crushing Area [Enter at own risk].

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The stoneshards on the ground and on nearby larger stones but into
you draining your blood and trashing your clothes. Maybe you should do
like the giants and get some revenge on the stone around you. The
dwarven workers would like some extra, free, personnel too.

Rooms.Description:
Stones in widely varied sizes lie scattered around in what seems to
be a totally devastated area. No vegetation is still alive in here
after the the treatment the giants have given this place. The ground is
covered with shards and you must be very careful not to cut yourself if
you  want to walk around in here. On the other hand, if you stay long
enough maybe some giants will want to give you some of their special
treatment. The crushing area expands further north and west and there
seem to be some kind of raw ore receiving zone west of you.

Exits.Description: Ore Crushing Area [Enter at own risk].
Ore Crushing Area [Enter at own risk].
Some kind of crude stone dump awaits you.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The stoneshards on the ground and on nearby larger stones bite into
you draining your blood and trashing your clothes. Maybe you should do
like the giants and get some revenge on the stone around you. The
dwarven workers would like some extra, free, personnel too.

Rooms.Description:
Stones in widely varied sizes lie scattered around in what seems to

you  want to walk around in here. On the other hand, if you stay long

treatment. The crushing area expands further south and east.

Exits.Description: Ore Crushing Area [Enter at own risk].
Ore Crushing Area [Enter at own risk].

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The stoneshards on the ground and on nearby larger stones bite into
you draining your blood and trashing your clothes. Maybe you should do
like the giants and get some revenge on the stone around you. The
dwarven workers would like some extra, free, personnel too.

Rooms.Name: Crude Ore Deposit
Rooms.Description:
Whenever a load of ore comes from the mines, they dump it at this
place through a chute from above. This is below their dumping place. A
very first halt for the metal to be. The guided tours have been
cancelled for now but might be taken up later if the economic increment
is large enough and when safety can be fully guaranteed, which it can
not be today. Too many villains sneaking around the premises.

Exits.Description: Ore Crushing Area [Enter at own risk].

There is no way for you to get back up there. The constant downfall
of too big boulders would easily crush any head or any other bodyparts
for that matter in a few seconds, so you better forget getting up there.
Should be a BIG orerich stone coming down any moment. Better start
moving.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
There is no way for you to get back up there. The constant downfall
of too big boulders would easily crush any head or any other bodyparts
for that matter in a few seconds, so you better forget getting up there.
Should be a BIG orerich stone coming down any moment. Better start
moving.

Rooms.Name: Lower Mixing Station
Rooms.Description:
Coal, limestone and crushed stone shove down through the metal grid
roof from the upper level of the mixing station. The healthiness level
in here is not a very high one. The cunning dwarfs have trapped a huge
earthworm in here and it has been integrated as a part of the mixing
process. It brutally devours anything, or anyone, coming within its
reach. A small set of steps leads up east of you and going west would take 
you onto the dog trail.

Exits.Description: A small stairway leads up to above.
A small trail starts, but getting there, through the worm, is hard.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
One has to blend the components that are headed to the furnace in
the correct way to get maximum efficiency. Dwarfs like maximum
efficiency.

Rooms.Name: Dog trail
Rooms.Description:
At the end of the gigantic earthworm, that has been fully integrated
into the mixing process, a perfect mix is continuously 'released'. There
usually are a few dwarfs with absolutely no sense of smell who stand here
shovelling up the 'creations' onto carrier baskets. The dogs carry these
baskets up the trail that leads to the top of the huge iron mill chimney.
Some devouring sounds can normally be heard from the east.

Exits.Description: Further up the trail.

Going to the other side of the mixing station is easier without the
worm.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The dwarfs shovel the worm production into baskets to make transport
up the chimney a lot easier. Not a nice job, but someone has to do it.

Rooms.Name: Dog trail
Rooms.Description:
The trail is too narrow for anyone larger than two well built dogs
with a double basket. The space needed for two fully loaded dogs carrying
their load to the chimney top to pass each other. The dogs do not seem to
complain about this treatment. Perhaps they get enough rewards for their
hard work to make up for all of it. Perhaps they get to eat captured
intruders...

Exits.Description: The trail continues.
The trail continues.

Rooms.Name: Upper part of the Dog trail
Rooms.Description:
A little intricately designed slope allows for the dogs to unload
themselves without getting hurt. The mix does not just accumulate on
the ground but rumbles eastwards and slightly downwards into the top of
the chimney. A slight rush of heat comes towards you every time a package
enters the chimney. Wonder what happens in there. Feel free to enter and
find out for yourself. But do not forget to close after you, leaking
gases can be troublesome. Or if strolling into chimneys is not your
thing, follow the trail down.

Exits.Description: Top of the furnace - The Furnace Throat.
Head down the trail.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The dogs step onto a little construct looking like a long AA. They
place the baskets on the A tops and kneel, where the baskets flip and
empty themselves onto the sloping inner sides of the A's. The load then
slides into the furnace without letting the heat out. Very simple.

It does not look that dangerous. Just a little peek inside would do
no harm.

Rooms.Name: The Furnace Throat
Rooms.Description:
The Furnace Throat has its own guardian, who carefully makes sure
that the from the west incoming mix is evenly distributed over the
chimney. As the mix accumulates and starts to dry up, it slowly descends
further down the furnace. It seems a bit hotter down there, but you could
surely handle that kind of treatment.

Exits.Description: Out to the Dog Trail.
Entering the Agglomeration Zone is a one way trip.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
As a first step in the iron melting process the base material is
loaded on top of a blast furnace to dry up and start the heating process
using warm gases from below. The setup of the material is essential to
get the best exchange values out of the process.

Rooms.Name: Agglomeration Zone
Rooms.Description:
The heat is increasing dramatically and the air supply decreases at
the same rate. The mix is slowly changing shape and the now completely
dry mix has started to agglomerate into larger pieces of increasingly
warmer clumps. You can if you want to, with the risk of slightly
scorching yourself, crawl even lower down to where the mix starts to
melt.

Exits.Description: The crawlway up is blocked by the slowly descending masses.
Pro Melting Zone. And do not expect to get up again.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
The gas coming from below not only dries and heats the mix, it also
starts to react with it. The reaction is called reduction. That is when
the oxides loose their bound oxygen and come closer to the pure metal.

Rooms.Name: Pro Melting Zone
Rooms.Description:
The heat is scorching and you can feel your skin peel as it keeps
getting warmer and warmer the deeper you go. Further down would be a
real killer. Looking at the walls you can detect small drops of molten
metal beginning to take form. Staying here too long can not be good for
you. You can overcome yourself and struggle further down but it is
not advised.

Exits.Description: The crawlway up is blocked by the slowly descending masses. Sorry!

The furnace shows only white metal and your nosehairs curl at the
temperature down there. Guess it is too hot for you.

ExtraDescriptions.Description:
As the reduction of the ore comes to a complete stage and only pure
metal is present, the very elevated temperature starts to have some real
effect on the metal structural state of existence and the melting
begins. Somewhere further down there must be an outlet so that the
molten metal can be extracted and give room for more ore in the furnace.

the background. If it was not for the continual moaning and grumbling

Mobs.Description:

makes that impression wither instantly. Arms, legs, hands, yes even
eyebrows are massive with muscles and nothing to mess with or insult.
There is not a single piece of fat anywhere, only muscles. His weight

The runner/carrier dogs are a combination of a huge Saint Bernard
and an even larger Irish setter. Four feet in height (with load) and
with muscles playing in their so powerful bodies they make up marvellous
creatures. The dog wears a large double cargo basket usually filled with

The eternally moving teeth of the unimaginably, enormous, tied up,
mutant sandworm would care less if you would get stuck in it or not.
Always fed with stone and ore it would devour you before even you
noticed it, no matter the thickness of your armour. Luckily for you (and
it) it is slightly less intelligent than a goldfish and just a tiny bit
smarter than its rear end.

Mobs.Description:
The giant mutated sandworm that is kept in the mill's lower region is
so incredibly large that its rear end takes up almost a whole room for
itself. That is good as the rear end has developed an intelligence of
its own (even though it surely is not much). Continuously extruding a
well digested menuer, it is most important that it is fed properly and
at all times. Its 'leavings' usually are taken care of with most caution

spends his time as a personal bodyguard to the master blacksmith (as if
the master himself needed it) and as his closest assistant in the
smithery. He sure does have the strength and stamina for the job even

complexion you really do not want to bug him with smart comments about
his lack of intelligence as you most certainly do not want this short

Mobs.Description:
This minor elemental is bonded in the uppermost part of the mill as a
first contact with the incoming mixture of ore preparing it for what to
come by continuously scorching it make it steam off any residual water.
As all elementals it is a bit undefined in its shape but it is grossly

Mobs.Description:
To compare this one with the preheating elemental is like to compare
a mild summer breeze with a volcanic eruption. One can see the stone
itself sweat from a bare look from the elemental and you are very sure
that stone does not have any glands for that. You can see that it is
more or less spherical in shape when it happens to stand still for more
than a fraction of a second. If the increase of elemental power
continues like this one can only but wonder what awaits you further down
the furnace...

The fire elemental shines brighter than the sun making it totally
impossible to look at but you can from the corner of your eye and
resisting the resulting pain see the flames coming out of its
body like a million blowtorches. Not only that, you sense that it is

Mobs.Description:
A fire elemental is bathing in a pool of smelt. It splashes around
and enjoys every second of it greatly. Not every day one find a pleased
elemental on this plane of existence. Better watch out so that is does
not invite you into its bath as it would most certainly scorch you very

Mobs.LongDescription: A soaking wet dwarf looks after the wellbeing of the water elementals.
Mobs.Description:
The charmer is keeping the water elementals healthy. That is his duty
in a short sentence. He does not really do anything else. He makes sure
the summoned cooling elementals are in full vigour and that they are
able and available to perform their duties. He also makes sure that the
control of these creatures is total as they most certainly will not like

Mobs.Description:
The Water elemental splashes down upon the molten metal drying it up.
Allowing for the workers to remove the bars so that a new batch of smelt
can be applied into the moulds. Unfortunately the water elementals are
severely hurt in the process as the smelt contains to much heat. Too bad
for them the charmers/summoners have them under total control otherwise
they would most certainly have done something completely different when
receiving that order.

Mobs.LongDescription: A dwarven worker removes bars from their moulds.
Mobs.Description:
The worker is dressed in dull grey clothing as all workers in the
mill but these carry the insignia of the foundry department on their
chests as well as the mill emblem on the shoulder pads. Their work is to
remove the newly solidified iron bars from their moulds and place them
in the bar storage. A job that would give most people pneumonia as it
varies so much in temperature from free running smelt to the constant
splashes of water elementals and small trips out of the room to the
outside and back again.

Mobs.LongDescription: The Master Smithy is one piece of compact dwarven power.
Mobs.Description:
No wonder this dwarf became a blacksmith. His technique is great when
wielding his hammer powerfully and with extreme precision in every blow.
Add to that a great planning skill for the development of tools (rural
as well as war) AND knowledge of the most ancient secrets of magic.
Combined with years and years of practise you get a master blacksmith,
one of the most respectful cunning persons you have ever met. Not
someone you would like as an enemy, if you ever would mess with
him he would most certainly mess you up REALLY bad.

His build is stocky as most other dwarfs but the arcane forces surge
strongly through this one. He wears no marking on his otherwise plain
clothing, but a simple brownish broosch with the official iron mill

whilst persuing their ultimate goal to destroy all stones bigger than
very very tiny. The dwarfs made a nice thing fooling them into this or
maybe the bribes were enough. They seem to enjoy it very much and they
